I wrote "Answer: Education & Reference is less common than Entertainment & Music" to `/work/answer.txt`. It is an estimate, not an exact count.

The file has no labels. The label names appear only in the instructions, twice each. So I could not count labels directly.

I classified the 835 questions with keyword matching instead. Entertainment keywords (movies, songs, bands, TV and similar) matched 97 questions. Education keywords (school, homework, definitions, grammar and similar) matched 47. A looser first pass gave 118 against 48, so the gap held up when I changed the keywords.

Keyword matching can misclassify questions. I did not read the questions one by one. The roughly two-to-one gap makes "less common" the likely answer, but the exact counts could differ.

I wrote "Answer: Education & Reference is less common than Entertainment & Music" to `/work/answer.txt`. It is an estimate, not an exact count.

The file has no labels. The label names appear only in the instructions, twice each. So I could not count labels directly.

I classified the 835 questions with keyword matching instead. Entertainment keywords (movies, songs, bands, TV and similar) matched 97 questions. Education keywords (school, homework, definitions, grammar and similar) matched 47. A looser first pass gave 118 against 48, so the gap held up when I changed the keywords.

Keyword matching can misclassify questions. I did not read the questions one by one. The roughly two-to-one gap makes "less common" the likely answer, but the exact counts could differ.
